mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines by at least 0.25% over the prior month, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate above 4.0% indicates deteriorating labor market conditions, signaling potential economic weakness and negative S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE rises above 4.0% within a month, or the signal's Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts and retail sales exceeding 0.5% month-over-month indicate a broad-based demand contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both decline > 0.5% MoM
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when HOUST and RSAFS both decline > 0.5% MoM, or the interaction signal's Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, rising industrial production signals robust supply growth and strong corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of late-cycle expansion periods when INDPRO rises, or the signal's Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: CPI inflation exceeding 3.5% per annum signals persistent price pressures that may trigger monetary tightening, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL exceeds 3.5%, or the signal's Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising federal funds rates and high inflation (CPI > 3.5%) indicates an active monetary tightening cycle, which typically depresses equity valuations and produces negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS rises > 0.25% and CPIAUCSL > 3.5%, or the interaction signal's Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a tight labor market, strong non-farm payrolls growth exceeding 0.5% month-over-month signals continued economic strength, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when PAYEMS growth > 0.5% MoM and labor market tightness is present, or the signal's Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained upward trend in industrial production indicates expanding supply capacity and improving corporate profitability, generating positive S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO rises, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year windows.
